_comment: Shared TS<->Rust set-signer for the GET /api/agents list face (#task:2195, batch 5).
This is a STRUCTURED DOMAIN seed, not an executable SQL script: it names domain
entities and their relationships with symbolic refs, and each side resolves those
refs to its own concrete ids. The TS half builds the world through the repository /
test-context builders (zero native SQL in the business test) and signs the expected
sets with the real agents.list() + canViewAgent; the Rust half builds a current-schema
fixture from the SAME structured facts. Both sides share ONE set of product facts +
expected ordered id sets, but NOT a database dialect.
One world holds every ACL arm so overlap and viewer-relativity are real, not isolated
per case. Each case pins the ORDERED visible-agent-id set (as refs) a viewer sees under
a (scope, stage-flags) intent — the load-bearing signal of the cold-read + core
`visible_agents` projector. The per-agent DTO projection is NOT re-checked here; GET
/api/agents/:id already signs that.
`agents[].created_at` is the ORDER contract of AgentRepo.list() (created_at ASC, no id
tiebreak), so the ascending values below fix the asserted order; each side pins it.
Agents (ref -> creator, created_at, status):
a-creator   viewer  100 active   -- creator arm only (no pair, no shared ws)
a-pair      other   200 active   -- direct-pair arm with viewer only
a-workspace other   300 active   -- shared-workspace arm with viewer only
a-overlap   viewer  400 active   -- creator AND direct-pair with viewer (overlap)
a-none      other   500 active   -- invisible to viewer (visible to its creator)
a-failed    viewer  600 failed   -- creator arm, hidden by default stage set
a-pending   viewer  700 pending  -- creator arm, hidden by default stage set
